summary: The open AI model repository and developer inference ecosystem in 2026 centers on Hugging Face as the dominant hub, now hosting over two million models, though it remains highly concentrated—the top 200 models account for roughly 49.6% of all downloads while about half of all models have fewer than 200 downloads. Around this hub, a competitive layer of developer-facing inference APIs (Together AI, Fireworks AI, SiliconFlow, Replicate, DeepInfra, OpenRouter) offers low-cost, OpenAI-compatible serving, while local-first tools like Ollama and vLLM handle on-device and self-hosted deployment. Model families from Llama, DeepSeek, Qwen, and Mistral drive most adoption, with DeepSeek overtaking Mistral in cumulative Hugging Face downloads in January 2026.

platforms.name: Hugging Face
platforms.purpose: The central open repository and community hub for AI models, datasets, and demos (Spaces), plus a routed Inference Providers tier that connects to third-party serving backends.
platforms.model_count: ~2 million+ models (ecosystem highly concentrated; top 200 models ~49.6% of all downloads)
platforms.pricing: Free tier for public repos; PRO subscription (~$9/mo); Enterprise Hub plans; usage-based Inference Endpoints and Inference Providers (pay-per-use) with GPU Spaces billed hourly.
features: Largest model and dataset registry with Git-based versioning
Inference Providers that route to Together AI, Fireworks, and others
downloadsAllTime and community metrics, model cards, leaderboards
platforms.best_for: Researchers, ML engineers, and developers who want the broadest selection of open models, community collaboration, and flexible paths from experimentation to deployment.

platforms.name: Ollama
platforms.purpose: A local-first runtime that makes it trivial to download, run, and manage open LLMs on a personal machine or self-hosted server with a simple CLI and local API.
platforms.model_count: Curated library of hundreds of models/variants (Llama, DeepSeek, Qwen, Mistral, Gemma, Phi, etc.)
platforms.pricing: Free and open-source; cost is only your own hardware/compute (no per-token fees for local use).
features: Quantized GGUF models for consumer hardware
Easy integration with local app frameworks
platforms.best_for: Developers and privacy-conscious users who want to run open models locally for prototyping, offline use, or self-hosted apps without cloud costs.

platforms.name: Replicate
platforms.purpose: A developer platform for running and deploying open-source models via a simple pay-per-second API, including custom models packaged with Cog.
platforms.model_count: 50,000+ community and open-source models (LLMs, image, audio, video)
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-second of compute based on GPU/CPU hardware tier; no idle charges; some models priced per-run or per-output.
features: Cog packaging for reproducible custom model deployment
Strong support for image/video/audio generation models
Client libraries for Python, JavaScript, and HTTP
platforms.best_for: Developers and startups wanting to quickly ship apps around open-source models (especially multimodal/generative) without managing GPU infrastructure.

platforms.name: Together AI
platforms.purpose: A high-performance inference and fine-tuning cloud offering the lowest-cost LLM serving with an OpenAI-compatible API across a wide catalog of open models.
platforms.model_count: 200+ open models (Llama, DeepSeek, Qwen, Mistral, and more)
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-token for inference (competitive low-cost rates); per-GPU-hour for dedicated endpoints; usage-based fine-tuning.
platforms.best_for: Developers and teams running production LLM workloads who want low cost, scalability, and a drop-in OpenAI-compatible interface.

platforms.name: Fireworks AI
platforms.purpose: A speed-optimized inference platform for open models and compound AI systems, focused on low latency and high throughput for production deployments.
platforms.model_count: 100+ open models plus custom model hosting
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-token for serverless inference; per-GPU-hour for dedicated deployments; fine-tuning billed by usage.
features: Function calling and structured output support
LoRA fine-tuning and custom model hosting
platforms.best_for: Performance-sensitive production applications and teams building agentic or compound AI systems that need fast, scalable inference.

platforms.name: SiliconFlow
platforms.purpose: An all-in-one value-focused platform for both hosting and high-performance inference of open models, noted for fast inference at competitive cost.
platforms.model_count: Catalog of popular open LLMs and multimodal models (dozens to 100+)
platforms.pricing: Usage-based pay-per-token inference with cost-efficient rates; dedicated/managed hosting options.
features: Combined hosting and serving in one platform
Support for text, image, and multimodal models
platforms.best_for: Cost-conscious organizations and developers seeking the best balance of performance, price, and an all-in-one hosting-plus-inference solution.

platforms.name: DeepInfra
platforms.purpose: A low-cost serverless inference provider serving popular open models through a simple, OpenAI-compatible pay-per-token API.
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-token/per-use with aggressively low rates; dedicated GPU options available.
features: Broad model catalog including embeddings and speech
platforms.best_for: Developers prioritizing the lowest possible inference cost with minimal setup for standard open-model workloads.

platforms.name: OpenRouter
platforms.purpose: A unified API gateway/router that aggregates many model providers (open and proprietary) behind a single OpenAI-compatible endpoint with automatic routing and fallback.
platforms.model_count: 300+ models across dozens of providers (open and closed)
platforms.pricing: Pass-through usage-based pricing per model with a small routing margin; pay-as-you-go credits.
features: Single API for many providers and models
Automatic routing, fallback, and load balancing
Price and latency comparison across providers
Easy model swapping without code changes
platforms.best_for: Developers who want provider-agnostic access, resilience, and the ability to compare or switch between many models through one interface.

platforms.name: Modal
platforms.purpose: A Python-first serverless GPU compute platform giving developers full control to deploy models, run inference, and build custom ML pipelines.
platforms.model_count: Unlimited / bring-your-own (any model you package in code)
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-second serverless GPU/CPU compute; no charge when idle (scale-to-zero).
features: Full control over environment and dependencies
Suited for custom inference, batch jobs, and fine-tuning
platforms.best_for: ML engineers and teams that need full programmatic control and custom infrastructure rather than a fixed model catalog.

platforms.name: Baseten
platforms.purpose: A production-grade platform for deploying and serving ML models at scale, with a focus on reliability, autoscaling, and custom model deployment via Truss.
platforms.model_count: Bring-your-own plus a library of prebuilt/open model templates
platforms.pricing: Usage-based per-GPU-minute compute for dedicated deployments; model-specific pricing for managed options.
features: Truss framework for packaging and deploying models
Support for custom and open models
platforms.best_for: Teams moving custom or open models into production who need reliable, scalable, observable serving infrastructure.

platforms.name: RunPod
platforms.purpose: A cost-effective GPU cloud for raw GPU rental and serverless inference, letting developers run any model or workload on affordable on-demand hardware.
platforms.model_count: Bring-your-own (any model); templates for popular open models
platforms.pricing: Per-hour/per-second GPU rental (community and secure cloud tiers); serverless pay-per-use endpoints.
features: Low-cost on-demand and spot GPU rental
Prebuilt templates for common ML stacks
Full control over containers and environments
platforms.best_for: Developers and researchers needing affordable raw GPU compute or self-managed serving for custom and open models.

platforms.name: vLLM
platforms.purpose: An open-source, high-throughput inference and serving engine for LLMs, widely used for self-hosted GPU serving with efficient memory management.
platforms.model_count: Supports most Hugging Face transformer models
platforms.pricing: Free and open-source (self-hosted; you provide the GPU infrastructure).
features: PagedAttention for efficient KV-cache memory use
The de facto standard engine behind many hosted providers
platforms.best_for: Teams self-hosting LLMs on their own GPUs who need maximum throughput and control over the serving stack.
